correctness.rationale: For any nontrivial 2-cycle, the memory increment forces opposite x-coordinates. The two first-coordinate equations imply |v|+|v+u|=2(1-1/beta); the exact identity for shifted absolute values partitions all real states into precisely three disjoint interior sign cases plus shared endpoints. Strict monotonicity of beta*u^2/(2*cos(u)) for u<pi/2 and beta*u^2/(-2*cos(u)) for pi/2<u<2 establishes unique branch roots and their exact domains. The crossings at u=ell have one explicit midpoint, preventing double counting. The pi/2 resonance gives the forcing-independent orbit and Taylor expansion gives the pole constant. Independently calculated two-step Jacobians and the real Schur test prove the exact crossing sink criterion and the positive-ordinate expanding eigenvalue. The package checker passed 882 high-precision sample conditions; these finite tests are supporting reproducibility rather than proof of infinite completeness.

originality.rationale: The original FPFM2 paper was read in full and gives the exact absolute-value map, one plotted numerical parameter example, and no whole-plane 2-cycle classification or all-forcing phase boundary. The 2022 NFP2 construction is the closest same-modulus source, but its additive constant forcing is mathematically different from alpha*cos(x). Searchable exact prime-two classifications of rational Rulkov, Duffing and Bogdanov maps are not stronger statements about FPFM2, and do not imply the theorem. Targeted exact-model and threshold searches returned no covering result. Novelty is assessed against the inspected sources, not certified against all unindexed prior work.

value.rationale: A complete all-parameter, all-plane classification of the shortest possible periodic orbit of an established fixed-point-free map is a natural exact dynamical invariant. The threshold beta=4/(4-pi) separates finite-forcing annihilation from unconditional persistence, creates a force-independent locked orbit, and has an exact reciprocal parameter singularity. The separate sink criterion determines where a genuine attracting oscillation occurs, distinguishing existence from stability; the positive-y cycle is everywhere expanding. These are structural phase boundaries and motivated comparisons with published numerical dynamics, not isolated arithmetic checks or arbitrary parameter slices.
